# Operational COTS pressure and INLA--BRT assessment

The selected operational model is `operational_rrn_raw_plus_manta_state`.
It combines undated RRN event-season pressure with exact-date Manta evidence
available through February. The residual BRT is not added to the operational
ensemble because it improves reef-blocked interpolation but worsens
leave-one-event-out overall and severe-event error.

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(knitr)
})
source('../../src/lib/model_registry.R')
root <- project_root()
cots_dir <- file.path(root, 'output', 'prospective_cots_nowcast')
brt_dir <- file.path(root, 'output', 'inla_brt_residual_ensemble')
read_out <- function(dir, file) read_csv(file.path(dir, file), show_col_types = FALSE)
round_metrics <- function(x) x |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
```

## Information boundary

The COTS pressure state uses the undated RRN event-season density, which is
assumed to describe pressure before bleaching mortality, plus the event-year
hindcast probability. Exact-date Manta and culling evidence is restricted to
the end of February. Latest Manta density, the prior three-year peak and time
since that peak complement the RRN value. Raw density excess is
`max(density - 0.22, 0)`; 0.22 COTS/tow is the hindcast outbreak definition,
not a newly fitted threshold.

## COTS candidate validation

```{r}
cots_comparison <- read_out(cots_dir, 'model_comparison.csv') |>
  select(candidate, scheme, rmse, predictive_r2, severe_rmse,
         occurrence_brier, false_extreme_rate) |>
  round_metrics()
kable(cots_comparison,
      caption = 'RRN, Manta, culling and retrospective COTS candidates.')
```

![](../../output/fig/Fig-COTS-01_prospective_nowcast_validation_v001.png)

Relative to the prior raw interval reference, the selected raw RRN plus Manta
state improves event-held-out RMSE from 0.14891 to **0.14848**, predictive R2
from 0.296 to **0.300**, and severe RMSE from 0.3275 to **0.3267**.
Reef-blocked RMSE is 0.13958. It sacrifices only 0.00033 RMSE relative to the
aggregate-best Manta-only candidate while adding direct RRN pressure and a
better severe tail.

### Gannett positive control and culling context

![](../../output/fig/Fig-COTS-02_prospective_focal_controls_v001.png)

Gannett 2020 has dated latest Manta density of 0.24 COTS/tow and undated RRN
event-season pressure of 9.9 COTS/tow. Adding raw RRN pressure lifts its
held-out prediction from about 0.121 to **0.183**. The log hybrid reaches about
0.262 and has the best severe RMSE, but worsens aggregate event transfer; it is
retained as a severe-tail sensitivity.

The Cull sheet contains exact dates, dive effort and removals in four size
cohorts. It is targeted intervention evidence rather than a spatially
standardised abundance survey. Adding removals per dive and log effort slightly
worsens transfer, so culling is retained as ecological audit context only.

```{r}
cull_context <- read_out(cots_dir, 'cull_target_context.csv') |>
  arrange(desc(cull_total_prior1)) |>
  select(ReefID, ReefName, event_year, observed_mortality,
         cull_total_prior1, cull_dives_prior1, cull_removed_per_dive,
         manta_latest_density, cots_outbreak_probability) |>
  head(12) |>
  round_metrics()
kable(cull_context, caption = 'Largest preceding-year targeted culling contexts.')
```

## Residual BRT after explicit hazards

The candidate ensemble is the bounded sum of the explicit-hazard INLA
prediction and a BRT fitted to its residual. Both the BRT and blend weight are
trained inside each outer event-held-out or reef-blocked fold. A balanced
candidate and a candidate giving severe observations four times the weight
were tested.

```{r}
ensemble_comparison <- read_out(brt_dir, 'model_comparison.csv') |>
  select(candidate, scheme, rmse, predictive_r2, severe_rmse,
         false_extreme_rate, mean_bias) |>
  round_metrics()
kable(ensemble_comparison,
      caption = 'Nested validation of INLA and residual-BRT candidates.')
```

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-01_inla_brt_validation_v001.png)

The balanced BRT improves reef-blocked RMSE from 0.13958 to **0.13666** and
severe RMSE from 0.28506 to **0.27452**, but worsens event-held-out RMSE to
0.14923 and severe RMSE to 0.33218. Severe weighting worsens event-held-out
severe RMSE further to 0.33585 and raises the reef-blocked false-extreme rate.
Neither candidate passes promotion.

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-02_event_performance_v001.png)

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-03_heldout_calibration_v001.png)

```{r}
weights <- read_out(brt_dir, 'blend_weights.csv') |>
  filter(scheme == 'leave_one_event_out') |>
  select(candidate, held_out_event = fold, blend_weight) |>
  round_metrics()
kable(weights, caption = 'Blend weights learned without the held-out event.')
```

The blend weight is zero for 2016, 2017, 2020 and 2022. Only 2024 receives a
non-zero correction, and that correction worsens its held-out score. The BRT
therefore leaves the low-mortality La Nina events unchanged but also cannot
improve Gannett.

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-04_severe_controls_v001.png)

## What the residual BRT is learning

Non-structural predictors with absolute Spearman correlation above 0.8 were
reduced before fitting. The screen removed redundant heat-history, SST-shape,
chlorophyll/Secchi and latitude/longitude alternatives.

```{r}
screen <- read_out(brt_dir, 'collinearity_screen.csv')
kable(screen, caption = 'Outcome-free collinearity screen for the residual BRT.')
```

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-05_residual_brt_importance_v001.png)

![](../../output/fig/Fig-ENS-06_residual_brt_partial_dependence_v001.png)

Rainfall, the base INLA prediction, starting cover and SST skewness are among
the strongest residual signals. These plots are useful for finding missing
mechanisms, but the failed event-held-out test means they are not yet a safe
new-event correction. The BRT remains diagnostic and may be reconsidered as a
separately labelled within-event spatial update.
